item.statement: The model explaining high coercivity via magnetocrystalline anisotropy shows only a partial fit to the experimental data trend.
quotes: Although the slope of the data set for fcc HEAs exhibits a slight deviation from that of the guideline, it is apparent that magnetocrystalline anisotropy partially accounts for the observed experimental trend.

item.statement: The exact origin of the additional ferromagnetic ordering at 168 K in the fcc phase requires further detailed investigation.
quotes: The high-field magnetization experiences a rapid augmentation as the temperature descends from 300 to 100 K, suggesting the consistency with additional FM ordering in the fcc phase, although a more detailed investigation is required.
The emergence of the 214 K transition is attributed to the influence of the C14 phase.
The high-temperature ordering at 1084 K is associated with the fcc phase, which exhibits an additional ferromagnetic ordering at 168 K.

item.statement: There is a negative correlation between coercivity (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms) in the fcc phase, where increasing Hc comes at the cost of reduced Ms.
quotes: The discussion would be useful for manipulating the fundamental magnetic properties of fcc HEAs based on FeCoNi.

item.statement: The parasitic magnetic transition observed at 58 K in the C14-dominant alloy remains unassigned to a specific phase.
quotes: In the latter, despite the predominant presence of the C14 phase, the fcc phase persists.
The bifurcated nature of these anomalies, akin to that observed in dχdc/dT of FeCoNiTi, is noteworthy.

item.statement: Increasing Ni content to achieve high Curie temperature is limited by the risk of the alloy becoming paramagnetic.
quotes: This alloy remains paramagnetic down to 3 K, likely due to the high content of Ni (∼70 at. %).
